title: Logic
html:
Logic is a system in Oaklands used to create systems powered by advanced logic. This can be as simple as automating components of one's property, or as complex as something like calculators or displays.

Overview

All logic-related structures can be purchased from Alan's AutoLogistics, located on Finlay Island near the entrance to the Acid Wastes.

Logic structures can be separated into four loose groups:

  • Inputs, which generate a signal for a logic system;
  • Gates, which are used to compare signals;
  • Processors, which manipulate signals;
  • Outputs, which convert a logic signal into action.

All structures that can interact with logic feature small square ports on the side of the device. Depending on the device, there may be a single port, or multiple ports. Whether a port is treated as input or output is not known until a user attempts to run a wire to it.

A full list of structures is available at Category:Logic.

Signals

Logic components generate signals. Most human interface devices, such as the Switch and Slider, generate signals between 0 and 10. Specialized devices like the Weather Sensor emit signals at different scales. Components that accept a signal for output, such as the 14 Segment Display and Music Note, accept signals well above 10, necessitating the usage of specialized inputs and/or processors to achieve signals high enough to perform certain functions.

Wires

Wires instantly carry a signal from their origin to their destination. A wire can be placed anywhere on one's property as long as it is initially attached to a solid surface. Wires can also be run through solid objects. Wires can be given any color while they are being placed, though the entire run of wire will be one single color. A premade palette of colors is available to all players; completely custom colors, as well as the option to enable neon wiring, can be unlocked via purchasing the "Creative Wiring" game pass for 400 Robux. When running a wire, the user must terminate the wire by connecting it to another logic component, otherwise the entire wire will be deleted. Wires can be cloned and cut, but cannot be modified once they have been placed. Moving or destroying a structure with a wire attached to it will also destroy the wire.

Certain input components will inherit the color of the wire attached to it. These are usually human interface devices.
